solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: When expected, corporation brought about change

indicators.note: a ship brought about is turned round, so these letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ETA, estimated time of arrival, says when someone is expected
corporation is an old jokey word for a paunch, a TUM

explanation.surface: A company changed things at just the moment everyone expected it to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' turns ETATUM round. 'Corporation' looks like a business but is the old word for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to alter in form, so as a verb it is a synonym for change.

clue.text: Dark apparition ultimately enters like silent cattle?

indicators.note: one piece that enters another goes inside it, here the end letter going into the made-up word

parts.note: cattle that make no moo would be moo-less, a whimsical made-up word

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word apparition

explanation.surface: A ghostly shape slips into a herd of oddly quiet cows on a dark night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts the N from the end of 'apparition' inside the joke word MOO-LESS. The question mark flags that invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: A night with no moon showing is dark, so moonless works as an adjective for darkness.

clue.text: One wasn't at sea in cutter

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who never went to sea is serving aboard a cutter, a small sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' shuffles the letters of ONE WASNT. 'Cutter' looks like the boat but is a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a small woodworking saw for cutting joints, an example of a cutting tool.

clue.text: Sweet message curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed literally means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a tweet is a short message posted online

explanation.surface: A sweet note that has been cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee, a British word, means sentimentally pretty or quaint, an overly sweet manner.

clue.text: Greek character in either of two countries, heading off salamanders, say?

indicators.note: the Greek letter sits in the shortened country, so it is placed inside it
with its heading removed the word loses its first letter

parts.note: Zambia or Gambia, two African nations that both lose their first letter to give AMBIA
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person living in one of two countries sets off to study salamanders.
explanation.walkthrough: Zambia and Gambia both lose their first letter to the same AMBIA, so either country works.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphibia is the zoological class of amphibians; salamanders are one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Love partially skewed in this writer's dramatic work

indicators.note: the pieces sit in another, so they go inside it

parts.note: the setter's way of saying my
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

indicators.note: skewed means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer admits their love is only partly felt and somewhat bent in their play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' looks like an adverb on 'Love' but is the anagram fodder; 'skewed' gives RALITYPLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A morality play is a medieval drama teaching a moral lesson, a kind of stage work.

clue.text: Spot opening words?

definitions.meaning: a spot is a tricky situation
the formal greeting said on first meeting someone

explanation.surface: Pick out the words a speech begins with.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a polite introduction and an idiom for an awkward predicament.

clue.text: A very hot jacket?

parts.note: something extremely hot is one that blazes, yet the word also names a sports coat

explanation.definitionFit: A blazer is a smart jacket, often with a club badge, while literally a thing that blazes.

clue.text: Child who's top of the class gets nothing for sport

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI here
a kid is a child
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: The pupil who comes first in class wins no prize at games.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) is entered with the digit read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikido is a Japanese martial art practised as a sport.

clue.text: Something on pages in dictionary sounded as if coming from pen?

definitions.text: sounded as if coming from pen?

indicators.note: the printed substance sits in the dictionary, so it goes inside those letters

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
ink is what is printed on pages

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry that sounds as though written with a fountain pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pen' is not for writing but a pigpen, whose occupants grunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Oinked is the noise a pig makes, and pigs live in a pen or sty.

clue.text: Obstacle in hospital room, it's inferred?

indicators.note: the clue admits the instruction is only implied, flagging that the answer itself must be read as wordplay on the room

parts.note: the answer split in two and read as an instruction tells you to turn round some letters, giving a room on a hospital floor

explanation.surface: Something in a hospital room is implied to be blocking the way.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue, which 'it's inferred' hints at: DRAW BACK, taken as an instruction, turns DRAW round to WARD, the hospital room.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a disadvantage or hindrance, a synonym for an obstacle.

clue.text: I can't recall its description: case of amnesia dismissed, was that, wrongly?

indicators.note: done wrongly means put in the wrong order, so these letters are rearranged
the case of a word is its outer letters, the casing
dismissed says those outer letters are sent away

explanation.surface: Someone with memory loss struggles to recall what a thing was called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' and 'dismissed' strip the outer letters from AMNESIA, leaving MNESI; 'wrongly' shuffles that with WAS THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatsitsname is a filler said when you forget a name, so it describes the thing you cannot remember.

clue.text: Feline relationships mentioned?

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: links are connections or relationships

explanation.surface: A question about relationships among cats.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat, so it is an example of a feline.

clue.text: Where it's possible to stand forward, gathering praise

indicators.note: one piece gathering another holds it inside

parts.note: to forward a letter is to send it on
to hallow is to honour or praise as holy

explanation.surface: Someone stands at the front while collecting praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where it's possible to stand' suggests a venue, but it is the swimming pool's shallow part.
explanation.definitionFit: In a swimming pool the shallow end is the part where the water is low enough to stand.

clue.text: Have bread, however sandwiches served up — on this?

definitions.text: Have bread, however sandwiches served up — on this?

indicators.note: one piece sandwiching another holds it in the middle
in a down clue served up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: yet means however
to have food is to eat it
a roll is a small bread

explanation.surface: Bread and sandwiches are brought out on a wheeled cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns YET into TEY, read upwards in a down clue. The whole clue also describes what is on the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea trolley is a small wheeled cart from which tea, bread and sandwiches are served.

clue.text: —– locate satellite

parts.note: the blank dash in the clue is literally a space
to station something is to place or locate it

explanation.surface: A blank stands for where to put a satellite.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash at the start of the clue is a gap, read as a space.
explanation.definitionFit: A space station is a large crewed craft orbiting Earth, an artificial satellite.

clue.text: Steps taken with pair of instruments

parts.note: the horn is a brass musical instrument
a pipe is the second instrument of the pair, a simple wind instrument

explanation.surface: Dance moves performed alongside two musical instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornpipe is a lively solo dance associated with sailors, so its steps are the definition.

clue.text: Spring flower, evidence of winter and fall

parts.note: snow on the ground shows it is winter
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: A flower of spring shows the traces of winter and autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' tempts as the American season, but it is a drop.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowdrop is a small white bulb flowering in late winter and early spring.

clue.text: Exposed and miserable, in bits

parts.note: stripped means laid bare, exposed
down means low in spirits, miserable

explanation.surface: Someone left naked and wretched, falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' looks like the definition, but it is the first piece; the definition is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stripped down has been taken apart into its components, so it is in pieces.

clue.text: Rush like that towards the top in extraordinary show

indicators.note: one piece in another is put inside it
extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue moving towards the top means read upwards

parts.note: so means in that way, like that

explanation.surface: A dash to the front at an unusual performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towards the top' makes OS, read upwards in a down clue; 'extraordinary' gives SWOH.
explanation.definitionFit: A swoosh is a rushing sound or movement, so as a verb it means to rush past.

clue.text: US student at work on flier

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: in can mean at work, as in being in the office
a tern is a seabird, a flier

explanation.surface: An American student working on an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a pilot or plane; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US an intern is a medical graduate in training, a type of advanced student.

clue.text: Flying, we sit down having bagged a place nearest the wing?

indicators.note: bagging something means capturing it, so one piece is held within another
letters flying about are scattered, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Airline passengers sit after grabbing a seat beside the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' rearranges WE SIT DOWN into WINDOWSET, and 'having bagged' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: On a plane the window seat is beside the cabin wall, the spot closest to the wing.

clue.text: Recognise wobbly wheels, back end gone

indicators.note: something that wheels turns round, so these letters are read backwards
with the back end gone the final letter is removed

parts.note: wonky means unsteady, wobbly

explanation.surface: Spotting that the wheels wobble because the rear has dropped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back end gone' turns WONKY into WONK; 'wheels' then turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To know someone or something is to recognise them, a near synonym.

clue.text: Heavenly queen in godmother, apparently

indicators.note: the answer lies in the clue words, running across godmother and apparently

explanation.surface: A fairy godmother looks like the queen of heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was queen of the Greek gods on Olympus, the wife of Zeus.

clue.text: Reveal changes in government department after U-turn on the other side

indicators.note: a piece in another is placed inside it
a U-turn makes something face the opposite way, so these letters are reversed

parts.note: the FO is the Foreign Office, a UK government department

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A ministry reveals a change of policy after a U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after U-turn' gives OF and 'changes' gives VERLEA. The FO is the Foreign Office, a UK ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: Overleaf means on the reverse of the page, the other side of the sheet.

clue.text: Line, row next to me

indicators.note: next to means the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A queue: the row beside me.
explanation.definitionFit: A métier is one's trade or profession, a line of work.

clue.text: Sweetheart expected soon articulated something fruity?

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment

indicators.note: articulated means pronounced, so the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: due means expected shortly

explanation.surface: A sweetheart who is about to arrive says something suggestive.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeydew is a variety of melon, and so is a fruit.

clue.text: Reconciled, very happy

definitions.meaning: people who have ... are reconciled after a quarrel

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both settling a quarrel and, in northern British usage, being thrilled.
